A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TRAN-D study. Their methods, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-E are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic and real-world reconstruction experiments, efficiency measurements, segmentation results, and ablations in Tables 1-5 and the main and appendix figures.

after.justification: v3 retains the original reconstruction, efficiency, segmentation, and ablation results, including the supplementary experiments and qualitative outcomes.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same segmentation module, object-aware 2D Gaussian optimization and losses, and physics-based scene update with single-view refinement. Equation formatting differences do not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate nine synthetic ClearPose sequences, ten synthetic TRansPose sequences, and six real-world sequences. Object-removal scenarios, seen/unseen objects, and sparse-view coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the reconstruction, efficiency, view-count, and appendix segmentation comparisons. Edits from 3D-GS/2D-GS to 3DGS/2DGS and Dex-Nerf to Dex-NeRF only standardize names.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains six synthetic training views, 30 test views per state, and single-view post-change refinement for TRAN-D. Metrics, training budgets, baseline controls, and the 3/6/12-view evaluation protocol are unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 4-5 retain the view-count, object-aware-loss, and physics-simulation ablations. The supplementary segmentation examples, qualitative view-count analysis, and failure cases test the same questions with the same evidence.

E5.justification: Both use the same point-estimate reporting, including averages across 19 scenes in Table 3. Neither reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1-5 retain identical numerical values and result entries, and the qualitative findings are unchanged. Table 4 corrects boldface highlighting of existing scores; the numerical ordering itself does not change.

T1.justification: Equations 1-8 retain the same rendering definitions, distance calculations, variance losses, and combined objective. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about segmentation-guided reconstruction, obscured-region coverage, efficiency, and physics-assisted updates. The headline performance claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations of background suppression, obscured-region optimization, and physics simulation are unchanged. The conclusion and Appendix E retain the same limitations concerning segmentation quality, lighting, tracking, and restricted object dynamics.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same prompts, fine-tuning recipe, GPUs, learning-rate schedule, iteration counts, and simulation parameters. Code-access information is unchanged; the updated author contact is an author-block edit.

R1.justification: The same 44 references and related-work discussion are retained. The relationships to sparse-view reconstruction, Gaussian surface modeling, and transparent-object reconstruction are unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 updates Myung-Hwan Jeon's affiliation and email, standardizes several baseline names, and changes Figure 11's labels from Train scene/Test scene to Training view/Test view. The narrative and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 4 correctly bolds FSGS's 0.1466 instead of TRAN-D's 0.2053 for 12-view RMSE at t=1. Figure 10 swaps two RGB panels to match their segmentation masks, Figure 11 clarifies labels, and minor spacing changes occur. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects misleading best-result highlighting in Table 4 and mismatched RGB-to-mask pairings in Figure 10, improving the accuracy of the evidence presentation. These are useful but limited corrections; the methods, numerical results, analyses, and limitations remain unchanged.
